source_registry.title: Transakcje na polskim rynku VC w Q3 2026

claims.statement: PFR Ventures and Inovo.vc report PLN 407 million invested by 60 funds in 48 Polish innovative businesses in Q3 2026.
claims.temporal_scope: Q3 2026 and Q1-Q3 2026 as explicitly labelled

claims.statement: The same report states PLN 5.03 billion raised in the first nine months of 2026, materially influenced by first-half megarounds for ElevenLabs and ICEYE.
claims.temporal_scope: Q3 2026 and Q1-Q3 2026 as explicitly labelled

claims.statement: Funds supported by PFR Ventures participated in 25 Q3 transactions; public-private capital participated in 30 of the 48 transactions.
claims.temporal_scope: Q3 2026 and Q1-Q3 2026 as explicitly labelled

enumeration.limitations: Report-defined Polish-linked transaction population; not a census of Poland-headquartered startups. Offshore-headquartered companies appear in aggregates. Company totals, transactions and funds are different denominators; no company-level funding record was derived from the aggregate.

source_registry.title: Transakcje na polskim rynku VC w 2025

claims.statement: The 2025 report describes health-related innovations as 13.1% of observed transactions and identifies 11 biotechnology rounds exceeding PLN 80 million together.
The report identifies SaaS as the most common business model in its observed 2025 financed-company population.

enumeration.limitations: Transaction-sector statistics are historic report observations, not sector shares of all Polish startups. No row-level records copied.

claims.statement: The public report landing page describes the annual study as based on questionnaires completed by startup founders and CEOs during July and August.
The full 2025 report is offered through a purchase link; the report body and sample denominator were not acquired.

enumeration.limitations: Survey-based report, not a census. Sample size and regional/sector estimates not verified. Paid report was not purchased or copied.

source_registry.title: Startup Booster Poland – Smart UP – oferta dla startupów

claims.statement: The startup-facing Smart UP page lists a 17 June 2024 to 31 May 2026 application window and explicitly marks recruitment ended.
claims.temporal_scope: application window 2024-06-17 through 2026-05-31; closed as observed

claims.statement: The offer describes accelerator and post-accelerator support and an overall maximum grant of PLN 400,000 for eligible selected micro or small startups.
claims.temporal_scope: application window 2024-06-17 through 2026-05-31; closed as observed

claims.statement: The development routes listed include business/public-partner acceleration, VC readiness, sector-agnostic acceleration, Go Global, and Poland Prize soft landing for teams from abroad wishing to establish and grow a business in Poland.
claims.temporal_scope: application window 2024-06-17 through 2026-05-31; closed as observed

enumeration.limitations: Programme maximum is not a grant received by any company. Operator terms and path-specific limits require separate checks; Poland Prize is a PARP route, not a PAIH-operated funding round.

claims.statement: The startup-facing Startups Exchange offer lists applications from 23 September 2026 through 7 January 2028 and targets Polish startups with international potential.
The support ceiling is PLN 100,000 combining services and a grant; services may not exceed PLN 80,000 and a grant may be at most 25% of financed services.
The programme describes a domestic preparation phase and an overseas phase involving incubation, acceleration, mentoring, study visits or trade missions.
The displayed StartSmart CEE operator opens recruitment on 2026-12-07, after this research date; the umbrella programme date does not imply that this operator is already accepting applications.

enumeration.limitations: Displayed overall window does not prove any specific accelerator round is open on a given day. Support is services plus grant, not an equity investment or all-cash grant.

claims.statement: PFR Ventures describes programmes investing in VC and PE funds. This is intermediary fund financing rather than a direct startup grant application.
At review, Starter, Biznest, Otwarte Innowacje, KOFFI and CVC were labelled enrollment suspended; PFR Deep Tech and Innovate PL FoF were labelled ongoing/open.

PFR Deep Tech targets VC funds investing in areas including AI, quantum computing, defence, robotics, space and cybersecurity. PFR Biznest involves angel co-investors, while CVC requires corporate participation.

enumeration.limitations: Call status concerns fund-management teams, not startup fundraising availability; each programme's documentation still governs eligibility.

claims.statement: Warsaw Booster is described as a municipal accelerator connecting startups with local government, businesses and academic actors to develop and test technologies addressing city needs.
The page records an update on 7 July 2026.

enumeration.limitations: Publication_date is actually page update date, not launch date. A follow-up retrieval timed out. Cohort names and current application status were not extracted.

claims.statement: KPT ScaleUp Booster supports industrial and game-development startups, with prototype-oriented corporate collaboration and mentoring.
claims.temporal_scope: KPT ScaleUp Booster project 2024-02-01 through 2026-12-31; historic editions separately labelled

claims.statement: The project listing records a 1 February 2024 to 31 December 2026 project period and support up to PLN 300,000; its programme pages separate an industrial vertical from GAME DEV GoGlobal.
claims.temporal_scope: KPT ScaleUp Booster project 2024-02-01 through 2026-12-31; historic editions separately labelled

claims.statement: The same page contains historic ScaleUp editions and labelled cohort lists, providing a candidate-discovery route that must preserve edition and date.
claims.temporal_scope: KPT ScaleUp Booster project 2024-02-01 through 2026-12-31; historic editions separately labelled

enumeration.limitations: Project 'active' status does not establish current recruitment. Participant lists prove the labelled programme relation, not startup HQ or a funding-round investment. No cohort bulk copy performed.

claims.statement: ARAW identifies Startup Wrocław as its route to ecosystem news, a startup database, incubator and coworking information, and financing opportunities.
The page links to startupwroclaw.pl for the actual local ecosystem material.

enumeration.limitations: The linked startup database has not been enumerated. A civic listing establishes a discovery source, not HQ, incorporation or current status for every listed company.

claims.statement: PPNT is a partner in CREDIT4CE, which advertised a ClimateTech accelerator for September through November 2026 and technologies supporting decarbonisation.
claims.temporal_scope: September-November 2026 accelerator; applications closed by stated 2026-08-10 deadline

claims.statement: The notice describes a planned selection of 20 startups and an application deadline extended to 10 August 2026.
claims.temporal_scope: September-November 2026 accelerator; applications closed by stated 2026-08-10 deadline

claims.statement: Eligibility described on the page includes legal personality, ClimateTech relevance, TRL 4 or higher and headquarters in a participating Central European country.
claims.temporal_scope: September-November 2026 accelerator; applications closed by stated 2026-08-10 deadline

enumeration.limitations: 20 is planned programme capacity, not verified admissions, Polish participants or a national startup count.

claims.statement: Space3ac describes startup-corporate acceleration and a Gdańsk base.
Its stated traditional emphasis is downstream space technology, with wider IoT, AR/VR, smart-city, property, AI, hardware and software applications.
The page exposes previous-edition links for 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2020 and a separate Poland Prize route.

enumeration.limitations: An unpopulated countdown and promotional application links do not verify a current deadline. Historical cohorts are distinct from current offerings. Covers Gdańsk evidence; Gdynia and Sopot company populations remain unreviewed.

claims.statement: Startup Spark connects startup technologies with industrial customers for pilots in manufacturers' facilities and operations.
The observed page identifies Spark 4.0 Rethink as focused on green technologies and the circular economy.
The operator's page presents cumulative support figures since 2017; these are operator-reported programme totals and are not used as unique-company or national denominators.

enumeration.limitations: Current cohort enrollment requires the linked programme terms. Partners and pilot recipients must not be converted into startup investors. No cohort list enumeration performed.

claims.statement: Rawa.Ink is a municipal business incubator in Katowice offering coworking, a fab-lab setting, networking, learning, project-development and internationalisation support to startups and SMEs.

enumeration.limitations: Resident heading returned no company inventory; no Silesian startup population inferred. No personal contacts copied.

claims.statement: PARP's Startup Platforms programme supports development from registration to an MVP and validated business model, with a stated overarching application period from 18 March 2024 to 10 May 2027.
Applicants must be willing to establish a company in Eastern Poland; programme geography and eligibility must not be confused with the founders' current headquarters.
The displayed operator places include Rzeszów, Mielec, Kielce, Lublin, Stalowa Wola, Puławy, Białystok, Łomża, Suwałki and Radom. Individual operators have different current recruitment states.
Post-incubation funding up to PLN 600,000 is described as a separate competitive component IIa, not an automatic award for every incubation participant.

enumeration.limitations: Operator list reviewed as a regional coverage map, not an exhaustive startup list. No startup records accepted from this source. Overall window does not mean all platform intakes are open.

claims.statement: Inovo describes its focus as pre-seed/seed companies founded by people from CEE, including the diaspora globally.
The stated multi-sector interests include developer tools, AI/ML, data science, healthcare, SaaS-enabled marketplaces and enterprise software.
The site exposes portfolio and co-investor links useful for bounded discovery.

enumeration.limitations: Founder origin is distinct from company headquarters/incorporation. Portfolio and co-investor membership do not establish a specific funding event. No portfolio population enumerated.

claims.statement: OTB describes current focus areas as AI and novel computing, space technology and physical AI, with a dual-use emphasis.
Its portfolio cards expose company sites, founders, investment years and sometimes current stages, useful as identity leads.

enumeration.limitations: Cards labelled 'Investors' list OTB professionals; do not treat these as event investor-participant lists. A current stage is not the stage of every OTB investment. Non-Polish companies appear in the European portfolio.

claims.statement: Market One Capital describes European pre-seed and seed investing in platforms whose efficiency and market access benefit from network effects.
The page states initial investment amounts up to EUR 3 million and links to its portfolio.

enumeration.limitations: Strategy/ticket range is not a company funding event. The fund footer lists Luxembourg, illustrating why a Polish investment network must not be equated with Polish incorporation or HQ.

claims.statement: SMOK describes early-stage investing in CEE and the diaspora, with Poland as its key geography and a preference for substantial CEE connections.
claims.temporal_scope: strategy observed 2026-11-18; portfolio statistic explicitly July 2026

claims.statement: The FAQ says software development tools and AI account for about half its investments, while also naming a wider set of sectors.
claims.temporal_scope: strategy observed 2026-11-18; portfolio statistic explicitly July 2026

claims.statement: As of July 2026 it reports 61 portfolio investments, then mixes 28 Poland-headquartered companies, 24 Delaware C-Corps, two Estonia companies and seven other CEE companies in its geographic description.
claims.temporal_scope: strategy observed 2026-11-18; portfolio statistic explicitly July 2026

enumeration.limitations: The 61 figure is SMOK's own investments denominator, not Poland's startup population. HQ and legal domicile are mixed in its category labels and must not be normalized into a homogeneous country split.

claims.statement: Innovation Nest describes a Europe-wide B2B SaaS investment focus.
The page explicitly states follow-on mode: investments are exclusively in existing portfolio companies and new investment proposals or unsolicited dealflow are not being accepted.
Its listed portfolio themes include marketing technology, fintech, hardware management, HR and medical technology.

enumeration.limitations: Preserve follow-on-only status as an observed current state; do not describe it as open for new startup applications. Portfolio membership is not event-level participation.

claims.statement: SpeedUp states that it currently does not undertake new investment projects and instead manages and supports existing active funds through their life cycles.
It points to S20 Fund, formed by some SpeedUp partners, as an independent platform undertaking new investments.
Individual group funds have different lifecycle states; for example Energy Innovation is described as doing follow-ons.

enumeration.limitations: S20 is a distinct platform, not an automatically interchangeable alias. Historic portfolio membership does not imply current funding availability or a new transaction.

claims.statement: ffVC describes a Warsaw-based European Tech and Gaming fund alongside its US funds, targeting Central Europe.
The Europe section emphasizes a Polish footprint and globally deployed products in e-commerce, fintech, gaming, cybersecurity, enterprise software and AI/big-data.

enumeration.limitations: Separate European fund and US/global firm identities; listed ticket ranges and partnership descriptions are not company-specific transactions.

claims.statement: bValue describes technology investing across Central and Eastern Europe and exposes separate Venture and Growth portfolio routes.
The current official home page provides dated investment-news links for further source-by-source event verification.

enumeration.limitations: The initially attempted bvalue.vc address returned 502; canonical current site was found through search. Venture and growth holdings must be distinguished and portfolio membership must not supply a funding-round date or amount.

claims.statement: The index lists quarterly reports for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026, with Q3 dated 21 October 2026.

enumeration.limitations: Index is a report-discovery route; no underlying company population or complete transaction table was enumerated.
